subject: Extending besag model to include extra level of random effects

messages.author: 461a0c7d7557dffc
messages.subject: Extending besag model to include extra level of random effects
parts:
Dear list,

I'm working with a spatial dataset of 564 regions. I'm fitting series of "bym" models gradually extending them from no covariates to adjustment for several categorical covariates.

I'd like to add one more level to analyzed data - 71 regions of higher order (hospital service areas, generated by aggregating 564 base regions; ie. nested within).

What is the best strategy to handle such situation? Add "iid" model using ID of the 71 regions to the model? If yes - what is the proper interpretation of such component? 

Unfortunately I cannot share the dataset but tried to work through he issues using London suicides example where I aggregated boroughs into 5 regions (attached).

Any help will be much appreciated!

radek

parts:
Hi,

We fitted a similar model using WinBUGS many years ago. You will find more details here:

http://www.bias-project.org.uk/papers/BayesianSAE.pdf

Check section 4.2.


We used two CAR models at different administrative levels. I believe that a similar model can
be fitted with R-INLA. WinBUGS adds a sum-to-zero constain to both spatial effects.

Best,

Virgilio

messages.author: 461a0c7d7557dffc
messages.subject: Re: Extending besag model to include extra level of random effects
parts:
Old topic, but remembered about this question when I stumbled upon a paper that seems to implement something similar.

Seppä K, Rue H, Hakulinen T, Läärä E, Sillanpää MJ, Pitkäniemi J. Estimating multilevel regional variation in excess mortality of cancer patients using integrated nested Laplace approximation. Statistics in Medicine. 2019;38:778–791. https://doi.org/10.1002/sim.8010 

From the abstract:

We estimated standard deviations associated with variation (i) between hospital districts and (ii) between municipalities within hospital districts. 

Code in the appendix specifies model as:
...
f(hosp,model="iid",hyper=list(prec=sigma.prior))+ 
f(munic,model="bym",constr=TRUE,graph=munic.adj, 
...

Cheers,
Radek
